newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican public sector workers in wage protest.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican public sector workers in wage protest.

text.p: Thousands of South African public sector workers took to the streets on Friday in countrywide demonstrations in support of wage demands, union officials said.
Workers demonstrated in Pretoria, Cape Town, Durban, the Free State and in the Eastern Cape, where they handed over memorandums to government officials detailing their demands.

"Figures coming in from the Western Cape, Durban and Pretoria show that around 100,000 workers took part in the action," a National Education, Health and Allied Workers' Union (Nehawu) official told Reuters.
The South African Democratic Teachers' Union (Sadtu), the Police and Prisons Civil Rights Union (Popcru), Nehawu and the Institute of Public Servants all took part in the demonstrations.
The unions are demanding a nine percent across-the-board pay increase and a minimum wage of 1,750 rand ($385) a month, while the government is offering increases of 7.5 percent.
Unions are also demanding that a three-year agreement on restructuring and improvement of conditions of service be implemented.
Both Sadtu and Nehawu are affiliated to the country's largest trade union federation, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu), which has 1.9 million members.
Sadtu said this week that the four unions would consider a national strike if employers failed to respond positively to Friday's action. ($ = 4.547 South African Rand)
